comments.author: Jolly-Rip5973
comments.body:
That really depends on what type of artwork you are trying to produce. 

I am assuming for game design you aren't trying to make photo realism. 

The most powerful model for prompt adherence and and LORA training is Qwen2512 20B in my opinion. 

The New KREA2 12B is very powerful too. 

Budget model (lower end hardware) is Z-Image Turbo 6B. 

Best Edit Model is Flux Klien 9B. 

Best Low End Model for Anime type assets is Anima 2B.

All of these models are open source and free to use. 

If you told me what you were trying to produce specifically I could easily do it and pick the best model for the job. 

It's likely you will need a multi-stage workflow though.

replies.author: FarYogurtcloset8261
replies.body:
I need it for: 

1. my characters are going to be fully detailed.... not anime style, but artistic illustration. with very specific details. (sometimes, i would give it a base image and say it add stuff and change clothing)

2. uniquely detailed walls and floors (i want to use color code and describe everything. i need very precise control.

3. also i want some unoutlined style charcters. (could a bit like origami style)

soo according to this, what would be better?

replies.author: Jolly-Rip5973
replies.body:
You have two options probably 

1) Use Krea2 and come up with a very specific way to prompt for an art style.   
2) Use Qwen2512 or Krea2 and train a LoRA on the art style that you want to use. You will have to come up with coherent dataset to begin with though so you can train the style into the Ai. 

Option 2 gives you the most consistency since the LoRA will ensure that all generated images have the same coherent style. 

Option 2 is the approach that most AAA game studios are doing. 

This isn't all automatic though, a AAA studio will have human concept artist that make the image to train the Ai on. 

Often images which you generate need to be corrected too. So generally a artists might generate an image and then put it into illustrator or photoshop and clean it up. 

Option 3 maybe, go on [Civitai.com](http://Civitai.com) and find some LoRA that people have already trained and use those. You can mix LoRA files in generations. So if you found two that you like, you could set them each to 50 percent and get a mixed style. 

The only model that can do precise color codes Is Ideogram4. It's probably the most powerful model there is but damn is it slow man. Krea2 can probably take color codes but it won't be as precise but it will be MUCH faster. 

Ideogram is made for professional uses including game assets but don't have a free commercial use license unless sign up for their website but that's only $15.00 a month.   
[https://ideogram.ai/](https://ideogram.ai/)  


Krea2 is yours to use for free until you make more than 1 million dollar then your supposed to get license. You can run both these models on your local computer if you have fastest GPU with enough VRAM.  
[https://www.krea.ai/krea-2](https://www.krea.ai/krea-2)

All of the models I mentioned are free to use locally using comfyui.

replies.author: Jolly-Rip5973
replies.body:
Nah I mostly just do pin-up artwork for fun. 

I'm assuming you vibe coding.   
I'm honestly not a huge fan of the LLMs. 

I think best use for Ai is actually things like using it for game design assets or at specific steps in a professional workflow for animation or special effects. 

Code is brittle. If you can't code and program is too complex, the vibe coding is going to mess up... and needs to be manually corrected by an actual software engineer. 

Same with using image models. You get a slop and have need to some art training to judge the outputs and manually correct them. 

Having done video production for 20 years, I am used t thinking in terms of professional workflows.
